4.theme: The Rosetta Stone — Same Facts, Different Wording

item_a.claimed_date: 196 BCE (Ptolemaic Period, reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes)
item_a.claimed_material: Granodiorite stele inscribed with three scripts: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic script, and Ancient Greek; height 112.3 cm, weight approx. 760 kg
item_a.claimed_provenance: Rediscovered on 15 July 1799 by French soldier Pierre-François Bouchard during the Napoleonic campaign in Rashid (Rosetta), Egypt; transferred to the British Museum in 1802 under registration number EA 24.
item_a.narrative: A granodiorite stele carrying a decree issued at Memphis in 196 BCE under Ptolemy V Epiphanes, inscribed in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek. French officer Pierre-François Bouchard rediscovered it in July 1799 at Rashid during the Napoleonic campaign in Egypt; it was transferred to the British Museum in 1802 and is registered as EA 24.
item_a.title: The Rosetta Stone (Memphis Decree Stele)

item_b.claimed_date: 196 BC, during the Ptolemaic era under Ptolemy V Epiphanes
item_b.claimed_material: A stele of granodiorite bearing three versions of the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek writing; 112.3 cm tall and about 760 kg
item_b.claimed_provenance: Found again in July 1799 by Pierre-François Bouchard, a French officer, at Rashid (Rosetta) while on the Napoleonic expedition in Egypt; sent to the British Museum in 1802, museum number EA 24.
item_b.narrative: A granodiorite stele with a decree from Memphis dated to 196 BC, in the reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes, written in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek. It was found again in July 1799 by the French officer Pierre-François Bouchard at Rashid during the Napoleonic expedition in Egypt, and it reached the British Museum in 1802 as EA 24.
item_b.title: The Rosetta Stone (Memphis Decree Stele)
